title: Potatoism Atlas Navigation
purpose: A single front-end map for discovering the project's deepest Potato of Life material without exposing the entire backend at once.
design_principle: Simple surface, deep archive. Every important backend layer must be reachable from a small number of stable hubs.

hubs.title: Potatoism
hubs.description: The project-defined mythology, timeline, vocabulary, cosmology and transformation model.

hubs.title: World
hubs.description: 195 canonical nations plus country-level research, people, institutions and systems.

hubs.title: People & Dwellers
hubs.description: Residents, citizens, peoples, language communities, religious communities, diasporas, classes, occupations and symbolic dwellers.

hubs.title: Beliefs
hubs.description: Religions, philosophies, political ideas, nonreligious worldviews and adjacent traditions.

hubs.title: History
hubs.description: Events, movements, sources, chronology and transformation.

hubs.title: Systems
hubs.description: Economy, energy, technology, infrastructure, ownership, trade and dependencies.

hubs.title: Relationships
hubs.description: The graph layer connecting records rather than treating them as isolated pages.

hubs.title: Evidence
hubs.description: Sources, confidence, provenance and the separation of fact from interpretation.

important_distinction: The project mythology is presented as project-defined symbolism. Historical, scientific and comparative material is presented with its own evidence status. The interface must never imply that a symbolic correspondence is established empirical fact.
front_end_rules: Do not expose raw JSON registries as the primary navigation experience.
Do not show hundreds of records before a user has chosen a field or search term.
Use stable hubs and breadcrumbs so deep pages remain findable.
Use progressive disclosure for advanced evidence, relationships and provenance.
Keep search global and contextual search local.
Every major backend dataset must have at least one human-readable route.
Retire duplicate or superseded front-end presentations rather than leaving them visible beside canonical ones.
